comments.author: Otto Chr. Lawaetz Thygesen
comments.content: Den forpagter Jens Thygesen på Hesselballegård, som bliver omtalt, er min farfar (Jens Christoffer Thygesen, 1858-1935), som ganske rigtigt dengang var ungkarl, men som senere på året blev gift med min farmor og et par år senere købte Dalbygård ved Kolding, som han ejede til 1927). Han var helfætter til Cathrine Marie Juliane Wolf, som blev gift med Heinrich Christian Sofus Lawaetz. Det var min morfars forældre. Det gør min farfar til min morfars halvonkel og min far til min morfars halvfætter.

comments.author: Antonio Losada
comments.content:
Dear Mr. Olsen,
My name is Antonio Losada, from Valencia, Spain. Im officer at Generalitat Valenciana, the Regional Government for which Gudie made some filming works. I’m just picking up some information on different people I’ve worked, because I’m trying to write a book.
And, alas! I’ve just popped out your site and this lovely text about dearest Gudie. I had the pleasure and the honour to meet Ms Lawaetz by 1985, when she was appointed to film the documentary on El Tribunal de las Aguas and had the immense joy of sharing with her some short rides all over the Valencia Hinterland called l’Horta to get nice locations for the film. She was really nice to me -then a young man with a lot of energy and keen to learn-. Both went to and fro in my car, and had a lot of funny chats on a lot of different matters. When she finally filmed and edited the documentary, she gave to me, as a present, a reproduction of an ancient map of Valencia (XVIII century, Vicente Tosca) which I proudly show at home.
Best,
Antonio
